title: The Mauryan Empire: India's First Pan-Subcontinental State

questions.question: The Arthashastra, the great Mauryan treatise on statecraft, is attributed to:
questions.rationale: Kautilya, also called Chanakya or Vishnugupta, composed the 15-book Arthashastra; its manuscript was recovered and published by R. Shamasastry in 1909.

questions.question: Megasthenes, who described Pataliputra in his Indica, was the ambassador of:
questions.rationale: Megasthenes served as resident ambassador of Seleucus Nicator at Chandragupta's court after the treaty that exchanged the eastern satrapies for 500 war elephants.

questions.question: The treaty ending the Chandragupta-Seleucus war of about 305 BCE transferred which territory to the Mauryas?
questions.rationale: Seleucus ceded the eastern satrapies — Arachosia (Kandahar), Gedrosia (Makran), Paropamisadae (Kabul) — in return for 500 war elephants and a marriage alliance.

questions.question: The Brahmi script of the Ashokan edicts was deciphered in 1837 by:
questions.rationale: James Prinsep, an East India Company civil servant, deciphered Brahmi in 1837 — the breakthrough that made Ashoka a historical figure.

questions.question: The Kalinga war, recorded with remorse in the 13th Rock Edict, was fought in:
questions.rationale: The Kalinga war of 261 BCE left, by Ashoka's own count, 100,000 slain and 150,000 deported, and turned him to the policy of Dhamma.

questions.question: Which pair of Ashoka's children were sent as Buddhist missionaries to Sri Lanka?
questions.rationale: After the Third Buddhist Council at Pataliputra (250 BCE), Ashoka sent his son Mahendra and daughter Sanghamitra to convert Sri Lanka.

questions.question: Ashoka's own name 'Asoka' appears in the minor rock edicts found at:
questions.rationale: Most edicts call him Devanampiya Piyadasi; the name 'Asoka' was discovered only in 1915 at Maski (and later at Gujjara).

questions.question: Which Mauryan provincial capital was NOT correctly matched with its province?
questions.rationale: Suvarnagiri was the capital of Dakshinapatha, not Avantiratha, which was governed from Ujjain.

questions.question: In Mauryan administration, spies were known as:
questions.rationale: Gudhapurushas were the state's spies, stationary (sanstha) and wandering (sanchara), as detailed in the Arthashastra.

questions.question: The last Mauryan emperor, Brihadratha, was killed in 185 BCE by his commander-in-chief:
questions.rationale: Pushyamitra Shunga killed Brihadratha during a troop inspection in 185 BCE and founded the Shunga dynasty, ending Mauryan rule.
